summary: The study investigates hot-wire assisted ALD (HWALD) for depositing tungsten films using alternating pulses of WF6 and atomic hydrogen. The process involves a hot tungsten wire to generate atomic hydrogen through catalytic dissociation of molecular hydrogen. The study highlights the coexistence of CVD, etching, and ALD modes during deposition and discusses the influence of process parameters on these modes. The results show that optimal conditions can be achieved to maintain ALD mode with high tungsten purity.
evidence: Tungsten films were deposited by this method using alternating pulses of WF6 gas and atomic hydrogen (at-H). The latter was generated by catalytic dissociation of molecular hydrogen (H2) upon the hot-wire. The study highlights the coexistence of CVD, etching, and ALD modes during deposition and discusses the influence of process parameters on these modes. The results show that optimal conditions can be achieved to maintain ALD mode with high tungsten purity.
